question: Can moiré inhomogeneous disorder be pushed below the U scale (~10-20 meV)?
finding: YES at the single-trap level. Individual moiré-trapped interlayer excitons show <1 meV PL linewidth (low T); hBN encapsulation reaches the homogeneous limit ~2-5 meV. So the ~20 meV 'disorder floor' is ENSEMBLE (trap-to-trap) broadening, NOT a single-trap limit.
implication: Blockade needs a SINGLE emitter (one trap), not the ensemble. For a single moiré trap the inhomogeneous disorder is removed by addressing one site -> the RT linewidth reverts to the PHONON floor (Gamma_phonon ~6-15 meV, the same floor the whole bound rests on). Tight moiré confinement's U (approaching g_xx~6*E_b at the single-site limit) can plausibly exceed 0.71*Gamma_phonon. So the moiré/saturation leg is genuinely OPEN.
the_real_catch: It is a SINGLE-EMITTER architecture (like a quantum dot), not a scalable extended nonlinear medium. That trades against the spec's scalability/CMOS-integrability conditions -- a device-architecture question, not a materials cap. Blockade at a single moiré trap at RT is the concrete experiment.
caveats: The <1 meV linewidths are LOW TEMPERATURE; at RT the single-trap linewidth is phonon-limited (tens of meV possible).
Order-of-magnitude literature reading, not a computed single-trap RT linewidth.
